title: Measurement & Metrology

canonicalTerminology.definition: Measurement traceability is the property of a measurement result whereby it can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to measurement uncertainty.

claims.text: Reliable railway inspection depends on fit-for-purpose measuring equipment, controlled methods, traceability and understanding of uncertainty.
claims.applicabilityNote: Level-neutral educational statement; adapt depth without changing the canonical fact.

equations.limitation: Simplified teaching expression; uncertainty, corrections and calibration models may be required for formal metrology.

visualSpecs.purpose: Show measurement chain from reference to instrument to recorded result.

prohibitedUnsupportedClaims: Do not invent calibration intervals, tolerances or acceptance limits.
Do not present classroom measurements as conformity evidence.
